text: With only linear optics and photon-number detection (no ancillas), how many of the four Bell states can a Bell-state measurement unambiguously distinguish?
choices: Two of the four, capping the success probability at 1/2
None: Bell measurement is impossible with linear optics
explanation: Calsamiglia and Luetkenhaus (2001) showed linear optics plus photon counting distinguishes only two Bell states (|Psi+> and |Psi->), capping P_BSM at 1/2; ancilla photons boost this toward 1. A complete deterministic BSM (choice 1) is impossible without ancillas/nonlinearity, and the answer is neither three (choice 2) nor zero (choice 3).
